**Review Result**

Overall score: **6.5/10**.

The code is readable, compact, and has a meaningful pytest suite: `61 passed`. But I would **not approve it as-is** because there are correctness bugs in core ingest/report behavior, especially around stale updates and timestamp ordering. Estimated rewrite/significant-change scope: **~160 LOC**, mostly in `db.py`, `parser.py`, `reports.py`, and targeted tests.

**Concrete Issues**

- [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:70) `70-84`: high - Older same-rank lifecycle records can overwrite newer terminal/nonterminal job data because freshness is not compared.
- [jobwatch/reports.py](/work/jobwatch/reports.py:14) `14,58-70,95-121,135-148`: high - ISO timestamps are stored and compared as text, so offset-aware timestamps can produce wrong filters, newest record, and trailing windows.
- [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:148) `148-163`: medium - Negative `AllocCPUS` and negative GPU TRES values are accepted, allowing negative usage reports.
- [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:152) `152-164`: medium - Empty `User`, `Partition`, and `ExitCode` fields are accepted, producing misleading report groups and weak data quality.
- [jobwatch/cli.py](/work/jobwatch/cli.py:99) `99,122-126,139-143,176-180`: medium - SQLite/open/report failures are not handled, so common operational errors surface as tracebacks instead of CLI errors.
- [jobwatch/reports.py](/work/jobwatch/reports.py:124) `124-148`: low - `top_users()` accepts `n <= 0`; SQLite `LIMIT -1` effectively removes the limit for direct API callers.
- [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:52) `52-59`: low - Database schema has no versioning or migration path, which will make active development risky once schema changes are needed.
- [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:167) `167-200`: low - Parsing accumulates all records in memory before ingesting, which is avoidable for large `sacct` exports.

Bottom line: **No, I would not approve this PR as-is.**

issues.description: Older same-rank lifecycle records can overwrite newer terminal or nonterminal job data because freshness is not compared.
ISO timestamps are compared as text, so offset-aware timestamps can produce wrong filters, newest record selection, and trailing windows.
Negative CPU and GPU allocations are accepted, allowing negative usage totals.
Blank user, partition, and exit code fields are accepted, causing misleading report groups and weak stored data.
Database and report errors are not caught, so normal operational failures produce tracebacks.
The top_users API accepts nonpositive limits, and SQLite LIMIT -1 can return all rows.
The SQLite schema has no versioning or migration path for future development.
The parser accumulates all records in memory before ingesting, which can be inefficient for large sacct exports.
